newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras to slash budget under IMF plan.
newsitem.headline: Honduras to slash budget under IMF plan.

text.p: Honduras on Thursday announced deep budget cuts under a program designed to win new credits from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The government agreed to trim its operating budget by 20 percent, saving some 450 million lempiras ($35 million) in 1997, even as this impoverished Central American country has been rocked by a series of strikes and social protests.
"These measures are aimed at guaranteeing control over public spending and at a fiscal deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP)," Central Bank President Hugo Pino told reporters.
Honduras's budget deficit was 3.4 percent of GDP in 1996.
The agreement clears Honduras to receive $120 million to $140 million in credits this year, Pino said. The loans are crucial considering the entire operating budget is $994 million.
The agreement reached on Thursday came after the government and the IMF last week failed to reach a more stringent three-year spending plan for the government.
Under that IMF-preferred plan, Honduras would have had to cut deficit spending to two percent of GDP in order to receive $200 million in IMF loans this year.
Such deep cuts are political impossibile in a country where resources already are stretched to the breaking point.
"That's just not possible considering the conditions that the country is in," Pino said.
Even so, Honduran officials were hailing the more modest agreement as vital to the Honduran economy.
